item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 301743
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Wed Sep 30 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Nolo, located several hundred miles west of Lihue, Hawaii, on
Hurricane Rachel, located a couple hundred miles southwest of
Cabo Corrientes, Mexico, and on Tropical Depression Nineteen-E,
located over the western East Pacific.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form late this weekend or early next
week south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development,
and a tropical depression could form while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward to northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Wed Sep 30 2026 
ZCZC MIATCPEP3 ALL
TTAA00 KNHC DDHHMM
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM MST Wed Sep 30 2026
 
...RACHEL CONTINUES MOVING NORTHWESTWARD...
...NOAA HURRICANE HUNTER AIRCRAFT DATA INDICATES THE STORM IS
GETTING BETTER ORGANIZED...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.8N 108.0W
ABOUT 185 MI...300 KM SW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 310 MI...495 KM SSE OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...85 MPH...140 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 315 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...978 MB...28.88 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches of warnings in effect.
 
Interests in the southern portion of Baja California Sur should
monitor the progress of Rachel.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located
near latitude 18.8 North, longitude 108.0 West. Rachel is moving
toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h). A northwestward motion at
a slower forward speed is expected during the next day or two,
followed by a turn toward the west-northwest and west later this
week. On the forecast track, the center of Rachel is expected to
move away from mainland Mexico and pass south of the Baja California
Peninsula through Thursday.
 
Reports from an NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft indicate that 
maximum sustained winds are near 85 mph (140 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Rapid strengthening is expected today and tonight, and
Rachel could become a major hurricane within the next day or so.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The minimum central pressure based on the NOAA Hurricane Hunter 
aircraft data is 978 mb (28.88 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Gusts to tropical-storm force are possible along portions of
the coast of southwestern Mexico through tonight.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel is expected to produce additional rainfall totals 
of 2 to 4 inches, with isolated maximum storm totals of 12 inches, 
across coastal portions of the Mexican states of Guerrero, 
Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco. This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with 
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall 
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will affect the southwestern coast
of Mexico during the next couple of days and spread northward along
the coast of west-central Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula
through the end of the week. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven
 
NNNN

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 14
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Wed Sep 30 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 301456
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 AM MST Wed Sep 30 2026

Satellite imagery this morning shows that Rachel has a large and 
elliptical central dense overcast with cloud tops of colder than 
-80C.  The storm also has a lot of outer banding, particularly in 
the western semicircle. However, despite the well-organized 
appearance, shear analyses suggest the cyclone is still experiencing 
15-20 kt of easterly to northeasterly shear.  Satellite intensity 
estimates are currently in the 60-77 kt range, and the initial 
intensity is set at 75 kt based on these and continuity from the 
previous advisory.

The initial motion is northwestward or 315/8. Rachel continues to 
move along the southwestern side of a mid-tropospheric ridge over 
northern and central Mexico.  This ridge is weakening due to the 
effects of a large mid- to upper-level trough seen in water vapor 
imagery over the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. 
As this trough moves northeastward and weakens during the next 
couple of days, this should allow another ridge to build to the 
north of the tropical cyclone.  As a result, Rachel is forecast to 
turn west-northwest and pass well south of the Baja California 
Peninsula before continuing westward away from land. The new 
forecast track has minor nudges from the previous track, and it lies 
generally near the center of the track guidance envelope.

Environmental conditions appear favorable for strengthening through 
at least 48 h, and rapid strengthening is a possibility once the 
hurricane develops a tighter inner core. However, two possible 
negative influences include the ongoing shear and Rachel crossing a 
track of cooler water left by Polo. Later on the forecast period, 
decreasing sea surface temperatures under the forecast track and dry 
air entrainment could cause some weakening. The new intensity 
forecast is an update of the previous forecast, and it lies near the 
upper edge of the intensity guidance.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Although the core of Rachel is forecast to remain offshore of
Mexico and the coastal watches and warnings have been discontinued, 
wind gust of tropical-storm force are possible along portions of 
the coast of southwestern Mexico through tonight.
 
2. Outer bands from Rachel will bring locally heavy rainfall to 
portions of coastal southwest Mexico through Thursday. This rainfall 
may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in 
areas of steep terrain.
 
3. Large waves could produce life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions along the southwestern and west-central coast of Mexico
and the southern Baja California Peninsula during the next several
days.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Advisory Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP192026
200 PM PDT Wed Sep 30 2026
 
...DEPRESSION FORECAST TO BECOME A REMNANT LOW TOMORROW...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.9N 127.0W
ABOUT 1245 MI...2005 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...30 MPH...45 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...E OR 80 DEGREES AT 14 MPH...22 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Nineteen-E was located near latitude 14.9 North, longitude 127.0
West. The depression is moving toward the east near 14 mph (22 
km/h). An eastward to east-northeastward motion is expected over the
next day or so.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 30 mph (45 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast during the next day or so, 
and this system is expected to degenerate into a post-tropical 
remnant low by late Thursday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Wed Sep 30 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 302033
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Discussion Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP192026
200 PM PDT Wed Sep 30 2026

Although the depression has a well-defined circulation, convection 
has fallen apart this afternoon, with the low-level circulation 
almost totally exposed.  Satellite intensity estimates are falling 
again, so the initial wind speed is set to 25 kt using a blend of 
the objective and subjective values.  

The depression is moving eastward at about 12 kt.  This general 
motion is expected during the next couple of days as the depression 
moves south of the remnants of Odalys and eventually starts to move 
on the southwestern side of Rachel's much larger circulation.  The 
track forecast is shifted a little to the north, mostly based on 
a more precise initial positions from visible satellite images.

Little change in intensity is shown for the depression due to 
moderate shear and plentiful dry mid-level air, somewhat countered 
by warming SSTs.  The shear is forecast to increase somewhat along 
with a bit drier mid-level environment, which is likely to bring an 
end to any organized convection.  Thus, the depression is forecast 
to become a remnant low in about 24 hours, similar to the latest 
global models simulated satellite data.  I will just mention some 
of the guidance is showing some re-intensification on Thursday, but 
that is deemed unlikely due to the unfavorable environmental 
factors listed above.
